newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors summon bankers over Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors summon bankers over Hanbo.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors summoned heads of two leading local banks on Tuesday over a loan scandal surrounding troubled Hanbo Steel Co, state radio said.
They are Sheen Kwang-shik of Korea First Bank and Woo Chan-mok of Cho Hung Bank, the radio said.

The Korea Broadcasting System said prosecutors would question the bankers on whether they received commissions in return for offering huge loans to Hanbo Steel which was declared insolvent on January 23.
It said the prosecutors also summoned Lee Hyung-koo, former president of the state-run Korea Development Bank, for similiar questioning.
Hanbo had accumulated about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions before it defaulted on debt repayments.
President Kim Young-sam, who ordered a thorough probe into the loans last week, has called the scandal a typical example of corruption.
